value.rationale: An approximated trailing factor is naturally available in row-split sparse least squares. A quantitative, sharp spectral and step-size frontier valid without conditioning assumptions is directly useful for reliable fixed-step design. The matched residual-map calculation shows a separate, qualitative failure that an arbitrarily good factor approximation cannot repair unless the true normal residual is used; thus the result gives an actionable distinction, not merely a scalar example or a restatement of classical least-squares stationarity. Explicit extremizers show the rate cannot be tightened without further assumptions.
